genericProblem: A non-production usability or list baseline can appear implemented while a local environment flag disables it, or while duplicate page-local defaults and repeated brand regions drift across consumers.
finiteDenominator: managed r5 DEV runner and formal seed manifest admission
the four OTP owner services that serialize debugVerificationCode
all platform-admin and operations-admin management-list initial page-size sources
counterexamples: Production must keep debugVerificationCode absent even after the non-production hard lock.
Candidate Select page sizes are not management-list initial page sizes.
Public invitation still requires the invite-bound mobile OTP; a retained invitation token is not authorization.

findings.evidence: The managed DEV runner maps an optional environment variable to false and the formal seed executor previously requires false, so a genuine owner debug response can be suppressed before the public UI receives it.
findings.minimumFix: A foundation policy forces true for non-production/UAT, and managed runner/seed manifest enforce the same true state.

findings.evidence: The two apps contain a finite set of local useState(20) and pageSize:20 management-list defaults.
findings.minimumFix: One foundation constant imported by every enumerated management list plus per-app denominator tests.

findings.evidence: Public invitation card header and h1 independently concatenate workspace and operations labels, while OTP notice/action surfaces have no grouping spacing.
findings.minimumFix: Fixed welcome header, logo plus operations-title heading, and grouped notices/right-aligned actions without changing owner protocol.
